lead.headline: US negotiators float Ukraine giving up the Donbas in exchange for Nato membership, Zelensky says
lead.short: US negotiators have raised the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday. "This was the first time this had been raised," he said. A US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed" but any deal would need both sides' agreement.

why.text: Nato membership has been Ukraine's goal and Russia's red line, so even floating it as a trade would change the shape of a deal.

more: Zelensky said that if he received a specific proposal with security guarantees, no limits on Ukraine's military and money to rebuild, he would put it to a referendum. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met him in Dublin on Thursday, after talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Russia controls most of the industrial Donbas.

Comments from Putin and Kremlin officials suggest Russia's position has not moved: it has demanded limits on Ukraine's army, territory and guaranteed neutrality, which Kyiv rejects. Other Nato members besides the US are wary of admitting Ukraine, and the Kremlin has always opposed it. Zelensky recently said the US mediators were pressing Kyiv to cede land to get a deal.

facts.Zelensky's condition: a referendum on any concrete proposal

update.new: The US floats Donbas for Nato membership.
update.front: For the first time, Washington has put Nato membership for Ukraine on the table, at a price.

seconds.headline: SpaceX catches Starship's upper stage with the launch tower's arms for the first time, after 14 orbits
seconds.short: SpaceX's 52m Starship upper stage returned from orbit on Saturday and descended into the mechanical arms of its Texas launch tower, the first time the company has caught it, ending a 22-hour mission in which it circled Earth 14 times. The planned double catch failed on Friday, when the Super Heavy booster was diverted and exploded in the Gulf.

why.text: Catching the upper stage is the step SpaceX needs to make Starship reusable like an aeroplane, and NASA is counting on it for the Moon.

more: The guidance system called off the booster catch because it "detected that the booster was not in the place it was supposed to be", spokesperson Dan Huot said; Elon Musk said it was also "slightly low on fuel". It was only the second time Starship has reached orbit. "Making more believers by the day," NASA administrator Jared Isaacman wrote on X.

NASA has contracted SpaceX and Jeff Bezos's Blue Origin for its plan to return humans to the Moon, due in 2028. Musk has said SpaceX will move to weekly and then twice-weekly Starship test flights, and has pushed plans to carry people to Mars.

facts.booster: diverted and exploded in the Gulf on Friday

update.front: SpaceX has caught Starship's upper stage, a first.

seconds.headline: An IndiGo flight to Guwahati returns to Pune after its landing gear fails to retract, and all 192 aboard are safe
seconds.short: IndiGo flight 6E 0623 from Pune to Guwahati, with 192 people on board, returned to Pune on Sunday after its landing gear failed to retract shortly after take-off. The Indian Air Force, which runs the airport, declared a full emergency. The plane landed safely at 9.04am after a low pass so the gear could be checked from the ground.

why.text: It is the latest in a string of IndiGo incidents this month, on India's busiest airline.

more: The pilot told air traffic control that the undercarriage had stayed extended, airport officials said in a statement, and fire services, ambulances and other emergency teams were put on high alert as a precaution. After landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay 7 by three fire engines and two ambulances.

Air traffic control withdrew the full emergency at 9.10am after confirming the aircraft was in a safe and normal condition. Earlier this month a Bengaluru-Lucknow IndiGo flight turned back after a hijack threat note was found on board, and another IndiGo plane made an emergency landing in Goa after an engine failure.

seconds.headline: More than 33,000 people ride the Pink Line on its first day, and riders get pink roses
seconds.short: More than 33,000 commuters used the Pink Line's elevated stretch from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere on Saturday, its first day of commercial service, figures show. Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda rode the first train at 6am and handed each first rider a pink rose. "It was flawless and smooth," he said.

why.text: The first-day numbers will shape how quickly the rest of the line, underground to MG Road and Nagawara, gets built.

more: Gowda said efforts would continue to take the Pink Line to M.G. Road and then Nagawara. Chief minister D.K. Shivakumar rode the line in the afternoon, spoke to passengers about their experience, and asked BMRCL to use Karnataka granite for its stations to support local industry.

Shivakumar also recalled riding with Narendra Modi at Friday's inauguration: "I did not have money with me when we went to buy the metro ticket. So I told him, 'You buy my ticket'. He swiped his card and bought my ticket too." "Let us compete in politics, but cooperate on development," he said, as the state and the Centre argue over who pays for the metro.

update.front: Bengaluru's new metro line has had its first day, and 33,000 people tried it.

stories.headline: An Israeli strike kills Samir Abu Younis, a Hamas commander who helped plan the 7 October attack
stories.short: Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade and one of the planners of the 7 October 2023 attack, was killed in an Israeli air strike on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in southern Gaza, Hamas and the Israeli military said. Witnesses said four missiles hit a tent in a camp sheltering hundreds of displaced people.

why.text: It shows the ceasefire in Gaza still allows Israeli strikes, a year after it was agreed.

more: The Israeli military said it took steps to "mitigate harm to civilians" and called Younis "a central figure among Hamas's senior figures". A medical source at Nasser Hospital said three injured people and one body had arrived there. Younis, 53, had led the brigade since 15 September and joined Hamas's armed wing in 1991. His funeral was due on Sunday in Khan Younis, Hamas said.

About 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage in the 7 October attack. More than 74,650 people have since been killed in Gaza, its health ministry says. A ceasefire was reached last October, but Israel continues occasional strikes it says target remaining Hamas militants.

facts.killed: Samir Abu Younis, 53, Rafah Brigade commander

update.new: Israel kills a senior Hamas commander.

stories.headline: Foreign investors put ₹84,290 crore into Indian shares in the first half of November, reversing two months of selling
stories.short: Foreign portfolio investors bought a net ₹84,290 crore of Indian shares from 2 to 13 November, depository data show, after pulling out ₹34,843 crore in October and ₹35,861 crore in September. Their net outflow for 2026 has narrowed to about ₹2.1 trillion from nearly ₹3 trillion a few weeks ago.

why.text: The return of foreign money has driven India's best fortnight in years, but analysts say it may not last.

more: "November's foreign buying is a sharp tactical turn, not yet a structural return," said Vedant Gupte of Trackk, adding that most of the money had gone into index heavyweights while domestic institutions booked profits. A sell-off in AI-linked stocks abroad pushed investors to look beyond technology-heavy markets, said Rohan Goyal of MIRA Money.

Falling oil, with Brent down around 13% in the first week of November, easing geopolitical worries and cheap large caps also helped, he said. Financials, telecom, capital goods, pharmaceuticals and carmakers saw the heaviest buying, Geojit's V.K. Vijayakumar said. Markets will watch the US Federal Reserve's minutes this week.

update.new: Fortnightly data show ₹84,290 crore of foreign buying.

stories.headline: Musk and more than 115,000 others sign a petition asking Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang
stories.short: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate its ousted chief executive Jensen Huang had more than 115,000 signatures by Saturday afternoon, including 5,965 current employees, 1,108 former employees and 63,063 shareholders, its website said. Elon Musk, Epic Games' Tim Sweeney, Replit's Amjad Masad and Y Combinator's Garry Tan are among the backers.

why.text: The company is split over its founder, with staff and shareholders pushing back against the board.

more: The petition says its signers are "concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process" and demands that the board "bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts". "Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," it says. It also calls for a fair investigation and more information for the public.

Huang left after reports of an affair with a chip executive whom US intelligence suspects of spying for China, and of other extramarital affairs. He has agreed to testify before Congress. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive while Nvidia searches for a replacement, and its shares fell sharply through the week.

update.new: A petition to bring Huang back.

stories.headline: Italy fines Meta €805m for reaching into 20 million Android users' photos without proper consent
stories.short: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805m ($887m) for accessing Android users' photos and videos without their specific consent, through a Facebook feature that suggests pictures from a phone's gallery as ideas for posts. It said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million users and gave it 60 days to switch the feature off by default.

why.text: It is one of the largest fines an Italian regulator has imposed on a tech company, over a feature most users never noticed.

more: Facebook asked for gallery access through a single app-wide permission, and the notice before it did not make clear what it would be used for, the regulator said. It weighed "the high number of people affected" and the fact that the practice is "still ongoing for those who have not updated the app".

"We strongly disagree with the assessment of the facts, its application of the law, and the disproportionate level of the fine," Meta told the BBC, adding that people must give permission on their device. Last month a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn after finding it had misled the public about Facebook user data.
